set_na_str_safe <- function(ft, na_str = '') {
  if (is.null(ft)) {
    return(ft)
  }
  ns_exports <- tryCatch(getNamespaceExports('flextable'), error = function(e) character(0))
  if ('na_str' %in% ns_exports) {
    return(flextable::na_str(ft, na_str = na_str))
  }
  if ('set_na_str' %in% ns_exports) {
    return(flextable::set_na_str(ft, na_str = na_str))
  }
  ft
}
format_table <- function(df, caption, digits = 2, font_size = 9, drop_model_type = TRUE, keep_together = FALSE) {
  if (drop_model_type && 'model_type' %in% names(df)) {
    df <- dplyr::select(df, -model_type)
  }
  if (any(c('part', '.part') %in% names(df))) {
    df <- dplyr::select(df, -dplyr::any_of(c('part', '.part')))
  }
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(~ gsub('^\\.', '', .x)) %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(~ gsub('_', ' ', .x)) %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(~ gsub('\\.', ' ', .x))
  pval_cols <- grep('p\\.value|p value|p-value', names(df), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  numeric_cols <- names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  round_cols <- setdiff(numeric_cols, pval_cols)
  if (length(round_cols) > 0) {
    df <- dplyr::mutate(df, dplyr::across(all_of(round_cols), ~ round(.x, digits)))
  }
  ft <- flextable::flextable(df)
  ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft, caption = caption)
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = font_size, part = 'all')
  ft <- flextable::autofit(ft)
  ft <- flextable::fit_to_width(ft, max_width = 6.5, unit = 'in')
  ft <- flextable::set_table_properties(
    ft,
    layout = 'fixed',
    opts_word = list(split = TRUE, keep_with_next = FALSE, repeat_headers = TRUE)
  )
  ft <- flextable::paginate(ft, init = keep_together, hdr_ftr = TRUE)
  ft <- set_na_str_safe(ft, na_str = '')
  ft
}
rename_outcome_model_columns <- function(df) {
  column_names <- names(df)
  column_names <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl('^Firth Logistic Regression.*Est', column_names) ~ 'Firth OR (95% CI)',
    grepl('^Firth Logistic Regression.*p', column_names) ~ 'Firth p',
    grepl('^Logistic Regression.*Est', column_names) ~ 'GLM OR (95% CI)',
    grepl('^Logistic Regression.*p', column_names) ~ 'GLM p',
    TRUE ~ column_names
  )
  names(df) <- column_names
  df
}
add_reference_row <- function(tbl, model, var, term_col = 'term', ref_label = NULL, digits = 2) {
  if (!is.data.frame(tbl) || is.null(model)) {
    return(tbl)
  }
  mf <- tryCatch(model.frame(model), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(mf) || !(var %in% names(mf))) {
    return(tbl)
  }
  var_data <- mf[[var]]
  if (!is.factor(var_data) || length(levels(var_data)) < 1) {
    return(tbl)
  }
  ref_level <- levels(var_data)[1]
  if (is.null(ref_label)) {
    ref_label <- paste0(var, ': ', ref_level, ' (ref)')
  }
  if (!(term_col %in% names(tbl))) {
    return(tbl)
  }
  estimate_label <- sprintf('%.*f [%.*f, %.*f]', digits, 1, digits, 1, digits, 1)
  ref_row <- as.list(rep(NA, ncol(tbl)))
  names(ref_row) <- names(tbl)
  ref_row[[term_col]] <- ref_label
  estimate_cols <- grep('estimate', names(tbl), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  if (length(estimate_cols) > 0) {
    ref_row[estimate_cols] <- estimate_label
  }
  p_cols <- grep('p\\.value|p value|p-value', names(tbl), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  if (length(p_cols) > 0) {
    ref_row[p_cols] <- NA_real_
  }
  term_vals <- tbl[[term_col]]
  if (is.factor(term_vals)) {
    term_vals <- as.character(term_vals)
  }
  var_rows <- which(grepl(paste0('^', var), term_vals))
  if (length(var_rows) > 0) {
    insert_after <- var_rows[1] - 1
  } else {
    intercept_rows <- which(grepl('intercept', tolower(term_vals)))
    insert_after <- if (length(intercept_rows) > 0) intercept_rows[1] else 0
  }
  if (insert_after <= 0) {
    tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(ref_row, tbl)
  } else if (insert_after >= nrow(tbl)) {
    tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(tbl, ref_row)
  } else {
    tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      tbl[seq_len(insert_after), , drop = FALSE],
      ref_row,
      tbl[(insert_after + 1):nrow(tbl), , drop = FALSE]
    )
  }
  tbl
}
format_p_value <- function(x, digits = 3, threshold = 0.001) {
  if (is.na(x) || !is.finite(x)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  if (x < threshold) {
    return(paste0('<', formatC(threshold, format = 'f', digits = digits)))
  }
  formatC(x, format = 'f', digits = digits)
}
format_p_columns <- function(df, digits = 3) {
  p_cols <- grep('p\\.value|p value|p-value', names(df), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  if (length(p_cols) == 0) {
    return(df)
  }
  parse_num <- function(v) {
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub('[^0-9eE.+-]', '', as.character(v))))
  }
  for (col in p_cols) {
    raw <- df[[col]]
    raw_chr <- as.character(raw)
    p_num <- parse_num(raw)
    has_lt <- grepl('<', raw_chr, fixed = TRUE)
    formatted <- ifelse(
      has_lt,
      paste0('<', formatC(0.001, format = 'f', digits = digits)),
      ifelse(
        is.na(p_num),
        raw_chr,
        vapply(p_num, format_p_value, character(1), digits = digits)
      )
    )
    df[[col]] <- formatted
  }
  df
}

filter_protocol_metrics <- function(df) {
  if (!all(c('.metric', '.estimator') %in% names(df))) {
    return(df)
  }
  # Keep only the prespecified OLS-based performance metrics used in this report.
  allowed <- c(
    'pearson_r_log10', 'rsq_log10', 'rmse_log10',
    'weighted_kappa_quadratic',
    'sens', 'spec', 'ppv', 'npv',
    'ols_intercept_log10', 'ols_slope_log10'
  )
  df <- dplyr::filter(df, .metric %in% allowed)
  df <- dplyr::filter(df, !(.metric %in% c('sens','spec','ppv','npv') & .estimator != 'binary'))
  df <- dplyr::filter(df, !(.metric %in% c('weighted_kappa_quadratic') & .estimator != 'weighted'))
  df <- dplyr::filter(df, !(.metric %in% c('ols_intercept_log10','ols_slope_log10') & .estimator != 'OLS_log10'))
  df <- dplyr::filter(df, !(.metric %in% c('pearson_r_log10') & .estimator != 'log10'))
  # Clarify category context for weighted kappa when threshold label is blank.
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      threshold_label = dplyr::if_else(
        .metric == 'weighted_kappa_quadratic' & (is.na(threshold_label) | threshold_label == ''),
        'NTproBNP categories: <100, 100-<200, 200-<1500, >=1500',
        threshold_label
      )
    )
  # Rename metrics to proper English and remove estimator column
  metric_labels <- c(
    'pearson_r_log10' = 'Pearson Correlation (log10)',
    'rsq_log10' = 'R-squared (log10)',
    'rmse_log10' = 'RMSE (log10)',
    'weighted_kappa_quadratic' = 'Weighted Kappa (Quadratic)',
    'sens' = 'Sensitivity',
    'spec' = 'Specificity',
    'ppv' = 'Positive Predictive Value',
    'npv' = 'Negative Predictive Value',
    'ols_intercept_log10' = 'Calibration Intercept (log10)',
    'ols_slope_log10' = 'Calibration Slope (log10)'
  )
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.metric = dplyr::recode(.metric, !!!metric_labels)) %>%
    dplyr::select(-.estimator) %>%
    dplyr::rename(Metric = .metric, Estimate = .estimate)
  df
}
format_validation_metrics <- function(validation_tbl) {
  if ('estimate' %in% names(validation_tbl) && !('.estimate' %in% names(validation_tbl))) {
    validation_tbl <- dplyr::rename(validation_tbl, .estimate = estimate)
  }
  if (!('ci_lower_95' %in% names(validation_tbl))) {
    validation_tbl$ci_lower_95 <- NA_real_
  }
  if (!('ci_upper_95' %in% names(validation_tbl))) {
    validation_tbl$ci_upper_95 <- NA_real_
  }
  metric_order <- c(
    'ols_intercept_log10',
    'ols_slope_log10',
    'pearson_r_log10',
    'rsq_log10',
    'sens',
    'spec',
    'ppv',
    'npv',
    'weighted_kappa_quadratic',
    'rmse_log10'
  )
  metric_labels <- c(
    'ols_intercept_log10' = 'Calibration Intercept (log10)',
    'ols_slope_log10' = 'Calibration Slope (log10)',
    'pearson_r_log10' = 'Pearson Correlation (log10)',
    'rsq_log10' = 'R-squared (log10)',
    'sens' = 'Sensitivity',
    'spec' = 'Specificity',
    'ppv' = 'Positive Predictive Value',
    'npv' = 'Negative Predictive Value',
    'weighted_kappa_quadratic' = 'Weighted Kappa (Quadratic)',
    'rmse_log10' = 'RMSE (log10)'
  )
  validation_tbl %>%
    dplyr::filter(.metric %in% metric_order) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      metric_order = factor(.metric, levels = metric_order),
      threshold_label = dplyr::case_when(
        .metric %in% c('sens', 'spec', 'ppv', 'npv') ~ 'NTproBNP >=300 vs <300',
        .metric == 'weighted_kappa_quadratic' ~ 'NTproBNP categories: <100, 100-<200, 200-<1500, >=1500',
        TRUE ~ ''
      ),
      Metric = dplyr::recode(.metric, !!!metric_labels)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(metric_order) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Metric,
      threshold_label,
      Estimate = .estimate,
      `95% CI Lower` = ci_lower_95,
      `95% CI Upper` = ci_upper_95
    )
}

    dplyr::filter(.metric %in% metric_order) %>%

        .metric %in% c('sens', 'spec', 'ppv', 'npv') ~ 'NTproBNP >=300 vs <300',
        .metric == 'weighted_kappa_quadratic' ~ 'NTproBNP categories: <100, 100-<200, 200-<1500, >=1500',
        TRUE ~ ''
      ),
      Metric = dplyr::recode(.metric, !!!metric_labels)

      Metric,
      threshold_label,
      Apparent = apparent_estimate,

      `Optimism-Corrected` = optimism_corrected,
      `95% CI Lower` = ci_lower_95,
      `95% CI Upper` = ci_upper_95

# Primary Analysis: Kasahara Conversion Formula
The Kasahara formula was applied to BNP values to predict NT-proBNP. Agreement between measured and predicted values is summarized below.

## Model definition, equation, and interpretation
The Kasahara conversion is an externally derived linear regression on the log10 scale that predicts the median NT-proBNP from BNP and covariates. Variables: BNP and NT-proBNP are in pg/mL; Age in years; BMI in kg/m^2; Hb_gdl in g/dL; CrCl in mL/min; Sex_M = 1 for male and 0 for female; AF = 1 if atrial fibrillation is present.

The published equation implemented here is:
$$
\log_{10}(\widehat{NTproBNP}) = 2.05 + 0.907 \log_{10}(BNP) - 0.00522 \cdot Age + 0.00283 \cdot BMI - 0.00866 \cdot Hb
$$
$$
- 0.0422 \cdot CrCl + 0.000530 \cdot CrCl^2 - 0.00000214 \cdot CrCl^3
$$
$$
- 0.00000278 \cdot \max(0, CrCl - 56.5)^3 + 0.00000621 \cdot \max(0, CrCl - 72.4)^3 - 0.00000133 \cdot \max(0, CrCl - 93.7)^3
$$
$$
+ 0.0164 \cdot (1 - Sex_M) + 0.194 \cdot AF
$$
where BNP and NT-proBNP are in pg/mL; Age in years; BMI in kg/m²; Hb in g/dL; CrCl in mL/min; Sex_M = 1 for male, 0 for female; AF = 1 if atrial fibrillation present. The median predicted NT-proBNP on the original scale is $\widehat{NTproBNP}_{median} = 10^{\eta}$ where $\eta$ is the right-hand side above.

## Log-log OLS recalibration for external validation
External validation of the original Kasahara model is assessed with a single OLS recalibration on the log10 scale:
$$
\log_{10}(NTproBNP) = I + S \times \log_{10}(\widehat{NTproBNP}_{Kasahara})
$$
where $I$ is calibration-in-the-large and $S$ is the calibration slope. Perfect calibration corresponds to $I=0$ and $S=1$. We report apparent performance with nonparametric bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.

# Kasahara Model Recalibration
The Kasahara model shows systematic miscalibration (underprediction) when applied to this study cohort. A simple log-log linear recalibration can correct this bias using only two parameters.

## Recalibration approach
Recalibration uses an intercept ($I$; calibration-in-the-large) and slope ($S$; calibration slope) on the log10 scale. Perfect calibration corresponds to $I=0$ and $S=1$. The full implementable conversion equation is shown once in the Final full conversion equation section.

# Nested Model Comparison: Value of Interactions
Per protocol, this section evaluates whether extending the model with interaction terms between creatinine clearance, age, and BNP improves prediction accuracy.

## Models compared
Three modeling approaches are compared:

1. **Recalibrated Kasahara**: The original Kasahara equation with a 2-parameter log-log recalibration ($I$, $S$)
2. **Kasahara-like (re-estimated)**: Same predictors as Kasahara (log10(BNP), Age, BMI, Hb, CrCl, Sex, AF), coefficients re-estimated on this study's data (additive model)
3. **Extended model**: Kasahara predictors with restricted cubic splines, plus the 3-way interaction between spline-transformed log10(BNP), Age, and CrCl: $rcs(\log_{10}(BNP)) \times rcs(Age) \times rcs(CrCl)$.

## Optimism-corrected performance
Model comparison is reported using optimism-corrected performance (preferred over apparent-only comparisons).

## Interpretation
The nested model comparison demonstrates that:

1. **Simple recalibration is highly effective**: The 2-parameter log-log recalibration of the Kasahara model substantially improves calibration and achieves most of the predictive performance of more complex approaches.

2. **Re-estimating all coefficients provides no benefit**: Refitting the Kasahara model on this study's data yields only a small improvement in R² over the recalibrated original equation with apparent performance and no improvement after correction for optimism.

3. **Spline interaction terms add minimal incremental value**: Adding the spline-transformed interaction structure between log10(BNP), Age, and CrCl yields only negligible R² improvement beyond the additive Kasahara-like model.

This supports using the simple recalibrated Kasahara model as the primary conversion approach.

# Recommended Conversion Formula
Based on the nested model comparison above, the recommended conversion formula is the simple 2-parameter recalibration of the Kasahara model. This approach achieves the vast majority of predictive performance without the complexity of re-estimating coefficients or adding interaction terms.

## Recalibration equation
The full implementable conversion equation (including all Kasahara components and recalibration parameters) is shown once in the Final full conversion equation section below.

## Rationale
This simple recalibration approach is preferred because:

1. **Parsimony**: Only 2 parameters (intercept and slope) need to be estimated, minimizing overfitting risk
2. **Transportability**: The original Kasahara coefficients remain fixed; only a calibration adjustment is applied
3. **Performance**: Optimism-corrected performance remains close to more complex models in the comparison section above
4. **Interpretability**: The recalibration parameters directly quantify the calibration-in-the-large ($I$) and calibration slope ($S$)

Perfect calibration corresponds to $I=0$ and $S=1$. Deviations indicate systematic differences between the development cohort (Kasahara) and the validation cohort (this study).

## Statistical methodology
A single OLS recalibration on the log10 scale is used throughout this report. All recalibrated predictions, threshold derivations, and outcome analyses are based on this one model.

## Final full conversion equation
For implementation portability, the full recalibrated Kasahara conversion equation is shown below in a single expression (all Kasahara components plus OLS recalibration parameters):

```{r full-conversion-equation, results='asis'}
metrics_path <- file.path(params$output_dir, 'kasahara_model_prediction_errors.rds')
if (file.exists(metrics_path)) {
  metrics_full <- readr::read_rds(metrics_path)
  I_full <- metrics_full %>%
    dplyr::filter(.metric == 'ols_intercept_log10') %>%
    dplyr::pull(.estimate)
  S_full <- metrics_full %>%
    dplyr::filter(.metric == 'ols_slope_log10') %>%
    dplyr::pull(.estimate)
  if (length(I_full) == 1 && length(S_full) == 1 && is.finite(I_full) && is.finite(S_full)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      '$$\\log_{10}(\\widehat{NTproBNP}_{recal}) = %.4f + %.4f \\times \\Big[2.05 + 0.907\\log_{10}(BNP) - 0.00522\\,Age + 0.00283\\,BMI - 0.00866\\,Hb - 0.0422\\,CrCl + 0.000530\\,CrCl^2 - 0.00000214\\,CrCl^3 - 0.00000278\\,\\max(0,CrCl-56.5)^3 + 0.00000621\\,\\max(0,CrCl-72.4)^3 - 0.00000133\\,\\max(0,CrCl-93.7)^3 + 0.0164\\,(1-Sex_M) + 0.194\\,AF\\Big]$$\n',
      I_full, S_full
    ))
    cat('$$\\widehat{NTproBNP}_{recal} = 10^{\\log_{10}(\\widehat{NTproBNP}_{recal})}$$\n')
  } else {
    cat('Final full conversion equation not available.\n')
  }
} else {
  cat('Final full conversion equation file not found.\n')
}
```

# Derived BNP Thresholds
To demonstrate clinical application, we derive BNP thresholds that correspond to established NT-proBNP decision points (100, 200, and 1500 pg/mL). Because BNP and NT-proBNP are not linearly related and the conversion depends on patient characteristics, these derived BNP thresholds vary by clinical profile.

## Methodology
For a given target NT-proBNP threshold, we numerically solve for the BNP value that produces that target when passed through the recalibrated Kasahara conversion formula with specified covariate values. The base case uses median values for continuous covariates (Age, BMI, CrCl, Hb), Female sex (Sex_M = 0), and no atrial fibrillation (AF = 0).

The recalibrated Kasahara formula combines the original Kasahara coefficients with the 2-parameter OLS recalibration (intercept $I$, slope $S$) estimated in this cohort. For each covariate profile, we numerically solve for the BNP value such that the final full conversion equation equals the target NT-proBNP.

## Sensitivity of BNP thresholds to patient characteristics
The table below shows how the derived BNP thresholds vary when individual patient characteristics are changed from their median/typical values. This demonstrates the effect modification by covariates in the conversion formula.

```{r table-bnp-thresholds}
threshold_path <- file.path(params$output_dir, 'bnp_threshold_sensitivity.rds')
if (file.exists(threshold_path)) {
  threshold_tbl <- readr::read_rds(threshold_path)
  # Check if new column structure (with individual covariate columns) or old Profile column
  if ('Age' %in% names(threshold_tbl)) {
    # New structure with individual columns
    threshold_display <- threshold_tbl %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Age, BMI, CrCl, Hb, Sex, AF,
        `BNP for NT-proBNP 100` = BNP_for_NT100,
        `BNP for NT-proBNP 200` = BNP_for_NT200,
        `BNP for NT-proBNP 1500` = BNP_for_NT1500
      )
  } else {
    # Old structure with Profile column
    threshold_display <- threshold_tbl %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Profile,
        `BNP for NT-proBNP 100` = BNP_for_NT100,
        `BNP for NT-proBNP 200` = BNP_for_NT200,
        `BNP for NT-proBNP 1500` = BNP_for_NT1500
      )
  }
  format_table(
    threshold_display,
    'Derived BNP thresholds (pg/mL) corresponding to NT-proBNP thresholds of 100, 200, and 1500 pg/mL for different patient profiles.',
    digits = 0,
    font_size = 8
  )
} else {
  cat('BNP threshold sensitivity table not found.\n')
}
```

## Interpretation
The variation in derived BNP thresholds across patient profiles reflects the complex, covariate-dependent relationship between BNP and NT-proBNP. Clinicians should consider patient characteristics when interpreting BNP values in relation to NT-proBNP-based decision thresholds. The base case (median covariate values) provides a reasonable starting point for typical patients, but the sensitivity analysis shows how these thresholds may shift for patients with extreme values of age, renal function, hemoglobin, or other covariates.

# Secondary Analysis: Outcome Associations
Logistic regression models evaluate associations between biomarker categories and the 30-day composite outcome.

## Logistic regression models (categorical predictors)
The outcome cohort is restricted to participants in the complete-case conversion-model cohort with nonmissing MINS30 and vascular_death. Missing outcomes are not imputed.

The composite outcome is defined as 1 if MINS30 == 1 or vascular_death == 1, and 0 otherwise. For each categorical biomarker, we fit:
$$
\operatorname{logit}\{P(outcome=1)\} = a_0 + \sum_{j=2}^{4} a_j \; I(Category=j)
$$
where the reference category is <100 pg/mL and the remaining categories are 100-<200, 200-<1500, and >=1500. Models are:

- Measured NT-proBNP categories
- Predicted NT-proBNP categories from the recalibrated model

Odds ratios are $\exp(a_j)$ relative to the reference. Firth logistic regression is also fit to reduce small-sample bias and mitigate separation; interpretation of coefficients and odds ratios is the same.

## Continuous spline models
To visualize continuous associations, we fit restricted cubic spline logistic regression models:
$$
\operatorname{logit}\{P(outcome=1)\} = a_0 + g(X)
$$
where $g(\cdot)$ is a restricted cubic spline with 3 knots for $X$ equal to measured NT-proBNP, measured BNP, or predicted NT-proBNP. The plotted curves show odds ratios relative to the 25th percentile of $X$ with 95% confidence bands.

## Results

```{r table-outcome-a}
model_a_glm <- get_obj('model_a_glm')
model_a_firth <- get_obj('model_a_firth')
if (!is.null(model_a_glm) && !is.null(model_a_firth)) {
  tbl_a <- modelsummary::modelsummary(
    list('Logistic Regression' = model_a_glm, 'Firth Logistic Regression' = model_a_firth),
    estimate = '{estimate} [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]',
    statistic = 'p.value',
    fmt = fmt_statistic(estimate = 2, conf.low = 2, conf.high = 2, p.value = 3),
    exponentiate = TRUE,
    gof_map = NA,
    output = 'data.frame',
    shape = term ~ model + statistic
  )
  # Remove intercept and format category labels
  tbl_a <- tbl_a %>%
    dplyr::filter(!grepl('Intercept', term, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      term = dplyr::case_when(
        grepl('100.*200', term) ~ '100 to <200',
        grepl('200.*1500', term) ~ '200 to <1500',
        grepl('1500|>=1500', term) ~ '>=1500',
        TRUE ~ term
      )
    )
  # Add reference row
  ref_row <- as.list(rep(NA, ncol(tbl_a)))
  names(ref_row) <- names(tbl_a)
  ref_row$term <- '<100 (reference)'
  estimate_cols <- grep('estimate|/ Est', names(tbl_a), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  if (length(estimate_cols) > 0) ref_row[estimate_cols] <- '1.00 [1.00, 1.00]'
  tbl_a <- dplyr::bind_rows(ref_row, tbl_a)
  tbl_a <- tbl_a %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of('part')) %>%
    dplyr::rename(`NT-proBNP Category` = term)
  tbl_a <- rename_outcome_model_columns(tbl_a)
  counts_path_a <- file.path(params$output_dir, 'ntprobnp_cat_summary.rds')
  if (file.exists(counts_path_a)) {
    counts_a <- readr::read_rds(counts_path_a) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        `NT-proBNP Category` = dplyr::case_when(
          Category == '<100' ~ '<100 (reference)',
          Category == '100-<200' ~ '100 to <200',
          Category == '200-<1500' ~ '200 to <1500',
          Category == '>=1500' ~ '>=1500',
          TRUE ~ as.character(Category)
        ),
        `events / n` = paste0(events, ' / ', n)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(`NT-proBNP Category`, `events / n`)
    tbl_a <- tbl_a %>%
      dplyr::left_join(counts_a, by = 'NT-proBNP Category') %>%
      dplyr::relocate(`events / n`, .after = `NT-proBNP Category`)
  }
  tbl_a <- format_p_columns(tbl_a, digits = 3)
  format_table(
    tbl_a,
    'Association between measured NT-proBNP categories and the composite outcome (odds ratios).',
    digits = 3,
    font_size = 8,
    drop_model_type = FALSE,
    keep_together = TRUE
  )
} else {
  cat('Measured NT-proBNP category outcome model not available.\n')
}
```

# Appendix: OLS versus Passing-Bablok Sensitivity
This sensitivity section is provided at the end for completeness. The primary analysis uses a single OLS log-log recalibration throughout.

## Why OLS was used as the primary method
1. **Model structure**: The Kasahara prediction is derived from multiple measured covariates (BNP, hemoglobin, renal function, etc.), not a direct one-to-one assay comparison.
2. **Methodological fit**: Passing-Bablok assumes proportional error in both variables (a method-comparison setting). Here, predicted NT-proBNP is a model-derived quantity from multiple covariates, so that assumption is not well matched to this recalibration problem.
3. **Empirical robustness**: In this dataset, OLS and Passing-Bablok produce very similar recalibrated performance.

## Recalibration parameter comparison (log10 scale)
```{r table-recal-params-comparison-end}
summary_rds <- file.path(params$output_dir, 'kasahara_loglog_calibration_summary.rds')
summary_csv <- file.path(params$output_dir, 'kasahara_loglog_calibration_summary.csv')
if (file.exists(summary_rds) || file.exists(summary_csv)) {
  recal_summary <- if (file.exists(summary_rds)) {
    readr::read_rds(summary_rds)
  } else {
    readr::read_csv(summary_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
  }
  params_tbl <- recal_summary %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Method = dplyr::case_when(
        method == 'PaBa' ~ 'Passing-Bablok',
        TRUE ~ as.character(method)
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Method,
      Intercept = intercept,
      `Intercept 95% CI Lower` = intercept_ci_lower,
      `Intercept 95% CI Upper` = intercept_ci_upper,
      Slope = slope,
      `Slope 95% CI Lower` = slope_ci_lower,
      `Slope 95% CI Upper` = slope_ci_upper,
      n
    )
  format_table(
    params_tbl,
    'Log-log recalibration parameters: OLS versus Passing-Bablok sensitivity comparison.',
    digits = 4,
    font_size = 8
  )
} else {
  cat('Recalibration parameter comparison data not found.\n')
}
```

## External validation performance comparison after recalibration
```{r table-recal-performance-comparison-end}
ols_recal_path <- file.path(params$output_dir, 'kasahara_model_prediction_errors_recal_ols.rds')
paba_recal_path <- file.path(params$output_dir, 'kasahara_model_prediction_errors_recal_paba.rds')
if (file.exists(ols_recal_path) && file.exists(paba_recal_path)) {
  perf_ols <- readr::read_rds(ols_recal_path) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.metric %in% c('rmse_log10', 'rsq_log10', 'pearson_r_log10', 'ols_intercept_log10', 'ols_slope_log10')) %>%
    dplyr::select(.metric, OLS = .estimate)
  perf_paba <- readr::read_rds(paba_recal_path) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.metric %in% c('rmse_log10', 'rsq_log10', 'pearson_r_log10', 'ols_intercept_log10', 'ols_slope_log10')) %>%
    dplyr::select(.metric, `Passing-Bablok` = .estimate)
  metric_labels <- c(
    'ols_intercept_log10' = 'Calibration Intercept (log10)',
    'ols_slope_log10' = 'Calibration Slope (log10)',
    'pearson_r_log10' = 'Pearson Correlation (log10)',
    'rsq_log10' = 'R-squared (log10)',
    'rmse_log10' = 'RMSE (log10)'
  )
  metric_order <- c('ols_intercept_log10', 'ols_slope_log10', 'pearson_r_log10', 'rsq_log10', 'rmse_log10')
  perf_tbl <- dplyr::left_join(perf_ols, perf_paba, by = '.metric') %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Metric = dplyr::recode(.metric, !!!metric_labels),
      .order = match(.metric, metric_order),
      Difference = OLS - `Passing-Bablok`
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(.order) %>%
    dplyr::select(Metric, OLS, `Passing-Bablok`, Difference)
  format_table(
    perf_tbl,
    'External validation performance after recalibration: OLS versus Passing-Bablok sensitivity comparison.',
    digits = 4,
    font_size = 8
  )
} else {
  cat('OLS/Passing-Bablok recalibrated performance files not found.\n')
}
```

In this dataset, differences between OLS and Passing-Bablok recalibration are small; this supports retaining OLS as the primary method while transparently reporting the sensitivity analysis.
